summary: Independently re-verified every claim in M4.2a-coder.json against real NVIDIA hardware (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), the pinned vendor/llama.cpp tree, and a from-scratch full-suite build. All GPU correctness/bit-identity numbers reproduce the coder's reported values essentially exactly (deterministic fixtures). The A/B perf ratio (0.505x) reproduced across 6 independent criterion samples, tightly clustered (0.5044-0.5050x), consistent with the coder's 0.505x claim well within the +/-10% run-to-run tolerance. All three spot-checked vendor citations (interception line :8239, coopmat block bounds :4090/:4212, stride_a=ne10) are byte-exact matches against vendor/llama.cpp @ 6b80c74f28. The LOC overage (~3186-3226 vs cap 2300, independently recomputed) is real, honestly disclosed, and not padding (matches established per-file fixture-duplication convention seen across M3.x precedent test files). AT-3004 (git-tracked check) now PASSES post-commit as predicted. One notable finding: AT-2996's claim that criterion's full sweep is 'prohibitively slow / ~20-30min' and was worked around via a separate one-shot measurement is only partially accurate as disclosed -- QA's own from-scratch run of the SAME criterion bench the coder shipped completed cleanly in under 11 minutes (the coder's committed CORRECTNESS_MEMO fix evidently already solves the slowness; an earlier attempt in the environment had hit a SIGKILL, but that appears to be stale/pre-memoization-fix evidence, not a defect in the final artifact) -- LOW severity, does not affect correctness or the verdict.

deviation_3_assessment_ggml_vk_guess_spl.claim: coder disclosed calling ggml_vk_guess_split_k inline in the guard (condition #8) since the `split_k` local isn't declared yet at the :8239 interception point
deviation_3_assessment_ggml_vk_guess_spl.verification: Read the real function ggml_vk_mul_mat_q_f16 (ggml-vulkan.cpp:8156-8260). CONFIRMED all variables the guard references (disable_split_k -- function param; ne01/ne10/ne11/ne12/ne13/r2/r3 -- all `const uint64_t` locals declared near the top of the function, well before :8239) are in scope at the interception point. CONFIRMED ggml_vk_guess_split_k (ggml-vulkan.cpp:7754) is a pure query function (reads ctx->device fields + its params only, VK_LOG_DEBUG macro aside, no writes) -- calling it a second time (once in the guard, once at its official :8252 site) is side-effect-free and architecturally sound. The patch's call signature `ggml_vk_guess_split_k(ctx, ne01, ne11, ne10, disable_split_k, pipeline)` matches the real signature `(ctx, m, n, k, disable_split_k, const vk_pipeline&)` exactly, including the implicit uint64_t->uint32_t narrowing already present at the stock call site (not a new warning class). VERDICT: no obvious compile-breaker found; the coder's honest 'best-effort, not compile-verified' framing is appropriate and not overstated.

storage_buffer_16bit_access_drop.claim: ggml variant correctly drops SPIR-V capability 4433 (StorageBuffer16BitAccess) vs the leader because B is retyped f32
storage_buffer_16bit_access_drop.verification: Re-ran `cargo test -p axc-driver --test compile_shared_examples -- at_2985 at_2987 at_2997` directly. AT-2987's actual assertions (read source, lines 2598-2628) precisely check: (1) no capability in ggml-not-in-leader (empty), (2) the leader-minus-ggml capability difference is EXACTLY [4433] and nothing else, (3) Float16 (cap 9) is still present in the ggml variant (required by the shared[f16] a_tile/b_tile + the f32_to_f16 staging convert), (4) coopmat metadata b_type stays F16 (the coopmat operand itself is unaffected -- only the SSBO source buffer's storage-class capability changes). All assertions pass. The eprintln's loose wording ('caps IDENTICAL to the M3.6 leader') is a minor cosmetic imprecision (the printed set genuinely excludes 4433) but the underlying programmatic check is precise and correct. VERDICT: the deviation is real, correctly diagnosed, and correctly tested -- not a bug.

one_shot_vs_criterion_methodology_equiva.claim: AT-2996's bench-file criterion sweep is prohibitively slow (~20-30min) at the A/B shape due to double CPU-oracle cost repeated per sample, so the coder additionally used a faster one-shot MIN-of-10 measurement to cross-validate
one_shot_vs_criterion_methodology_equiva.verification: The shipped bench file (resident_q4km_matmul_rb_f32acc_cached_ggml.rs) DOES contain a CORRECTNESS_MEMO (Mutex<BTreeMap>) that memoizes the CPU-oracle result per (kernel,shape) after the first invocation specifically to address this cost (source comment: 'the oracle IS still computed... on the FIRST invocation... subsequent invocations reuse the memoized correctness value'). QA's own from-scratch run of this exact bench via the shipped script completed cleanly end-to-end (cube sizes + the A/B shape, 6 full criterion sample cycles) in well under 11 minutes -- notably faster than the coder's disclosed 20-30min estimate, and without the SIGKILL failure an earlier/stale log in the environment showed. Both the criterion-native numbers (this run) and my separately-checked GPU dispatch tests are in tight agreement, so the coder's headline numbers are validated regardless of which exact code path produced them. VERDICT: the methodology-equivalence claim holds; the coder's slowness estimate appears conservative/stale (possibly measured before or without the memoization landing cleanly) but this is a LOW-severity documentation-accuracy nit, not a correctness or scope problem.
